neighbours.label: a relative 'who' that hands a story on to the next person's action ('passed to Steen, who scored', 'sent to the president, who would sign it'), as against a 'who' clause that only describes someone
fire: She crossed the ball to Martinez, who headed it into the net.
The letter was forwarded to the dean, who would decide the appeal.
He tossed the keys to his brother, who drove the van to the depot.
The file went to an editor who will check every quote by Friday.
The quarterback threw to Johnson, who ran it in for a touchdown.
They handed the samples to a technician, who froze them overnight.
The bill passed to the governor, who signed it the next morning.
Leave the package with the porter, who will bring it up to your room.
quiet: She crossed the ball to Martinez, a tall striker from Seville.
The woman who runs the bakery opens at six every morning.
He tossed the keys onto the table and sat down to eat.
Anyone who has visited the island loves its beaches.
The quarterback, a rookie from Ohio, had a quiet first half.
Children who read every day tend to write better essays.
The governor, who is sixty, grew up on a farm in Iowa.
The porter is an old man with a grey beard and a kind smile.

predictions: fire 0.5-0.8 on ' who' or the verb after it when something is passed to a person who then acts; descriptive 'the man who lives next door' and appositives without 'who' below 0.1
short: handoff 'who' to the next actor's action
notes: Card: ' who' x2 in hockey and rugby passes, 'who would have signed it', 'a member who will deliver them', 'from there', 'thence'. Probe: 'to Steen, who had inside position' 0.787, 'member who will deliver' 0.729, 'president, who would have signed' 0.719; 'to Steen, a tall defenseman' 0.071, 'The man who lives next door' 0.006.
